source: Data Science in the Cloud with Microsoft Azure Machine Learning and Python — Stephen F. Elston, O'Reilly, 62 PDF pages
page_numbering: PDF pages, counting the cover as 1. The book also prints its own numbers, offset by six — printed page 3 is PDF page 9 — and the book's own cross-references use the printed ones. Every number here is a PDF page, because that is what a chunk records and what a reader is sent to.
labelling_notes: Questions are written as a student would ask them, then the answer was located. Written the other way round — read a passage, paraphrase it into a question — the question inherits that passage's vocabulary and retrieval finds it for reasons that have nothing to do with being good at retrieval.

A figure is printed on the page after the text that introduces it. Figure 4 is announced on PDF page 13 and drawn on 14, so figure questions name both: the sentence saying what it shows and the figure itself are different chunks, and either can carry the answer.
expected_class records what the question is, not what the classifier currently returns. A disagreement is the finding, not a labelling error.

pairs.question: What is Azure ML Studio?
pairs.note: One sentence states it: models are built and tested in the web-based Azure ML Studio. A genuinely direct question, and the baseline for what an easy one scores.

pairs.question: Which Python distribution should I install to match Azure ML?
pairs.note: Stated once, under Working Between Azure ML and Spyder. The version matters and is easy to retrieve the surrounding advice without.

pairs.question: Which dataset does the worked example use?
pairs.note: Named under Downloads on page 8 and described again in Problem and Data Overview on 15. Either answers it; both together answer it well.

pairs.question: What are all the ways data can get into and out of Azure ML?
pairs.note: A six-item list on one page, so page recall is easy and the phrase check is what shows whether the whole list survived into the prompt.

pairs.question: How many ports does the Execute Python Script module have?
pairs.note: Phrased with 'how many', which is one of the forms the AGGREGATION rule actually matches — included to contrast with python-libraries, which is the same kind of question phrased in a way no rule catches.

pairs.question: Which Python libraries does this report use?
pairs.note: The question behind A-730. An aggregation by meaning that matches no AGGREGATION rule, so it falls through to DIRECT. The names are spread over many pages and concentrated on 21; phrase coverage measures this far better than page recall does, since a complete answer names the libraries rather than reaching every page that mentions one.

pairs.question: What are the steps for training a model in Azure ML?
pairs.note: A procedure, and there is no class for one. Labelled DIRECT because that is what a question no rule recognises truthfully is — this pair exists to measure the fallback, not to endorse it.

pairs.question: How do I publish a trained model as a web service?
pairs.note: Another procedure falling through to DIRECT. The button name is the actionable part and the easiest thing to lose.

pairs.question: What does the Cross Validation module do?
pairs.note: Defined in place on one page.

pairs.question: What is the difference between the Reader module and the Writer module?
pairs.note: The contrast is split across a page break — Reader is described on 11 and Writer on 12 — so an answer built from one page alone is half an answer that will not say so.

pairs.question: Why would I write code in Spyder rather than directly in Azure ML?
pairs.note: A reason question. No class covers those either; recorded as DIRECT for the same reason as the procedures.

pairs.question: What does Figure 4 show?
pairs.note: Announced on 13, drawn on 14. Unreachable at all before figures were chunked, so this pair is the regression test for that as much as a measure.

pairs.question: What does Figure 1 show?
pairs.note: Same shape as figure-4-workflow: sentence on 9, image on 10.

pairs.question: How can I filter rows with SQL inside an experiment?
pairs.note: The module name is what makes the answer usable, and the question does not contain it — deliberately, since a question carrying the answer's own vocabulary measures nothing.

pairs.question: Can I use Jupyter notebooks with Azure ML?
pairs.note: Mentioned in passing on page 9 with a forward reference, and answered properly on 59. Page 9 alone would look like a hit and give a much worse answer, which is what makes this pair worth having.

pairs.question: What does the report suggest doing about overfitting?
pairs.note: Sits immediately before the web service section on the same page, so it shares a page with publish-web-service and the two must not be confused for each other.

pairs.question: What are the main conclusions of this report?
pairs.note: The Summary section states them as a list. The only genuine SUMMARY pair the material supports.

pairs.question: What does this report say about deploying models on AWS SageMaker?
pairs.note: The report is about Azure and never mentions SageMaker. Finding nothing is the right answer. Without a pair like this the set cannot tell a system that abstains properly from one that never abstains, and every retrieval change would look like an improvement.
